sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Guilford County?
sections.html:
The Guilford County Tax Department values real estate and sends the bill, and it serves owners at two counters: 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point. Both are open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The county was established in 1771 and keeps a courthouse in each of its two big cities. Greensboro took over as county seat in 1808, according to the state encyclopedia. The Census Bureau estimated 562,234 residents on July 1, 2025, spread over 645.92 square miles of land, so a sale in Guilford can mean anything from a High Point row house to an acre lot near Summerfield.

Ways to pay a Guilford bill, as the Tax Department lists them:

  • Online or by phone through the Pay It portal at (336) 203-7795, with a 1.85% processing fee plus a $2 transaction fee.
  • By mail to Guilford County Tax Department, P.O. Box 70939, Charlotte, NC 28272-0939, with checks made out to the department.
  • At either counter with cash, check or card; cards carry a 2.35% fee plus $2. Gift cards are refused.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 reappraisal and moratorium change in Guilford County?
sections.html:
The 2026 bill was calculated on 2025 values, and the new reappraisal values first show up on the 2027 bill. Senate Bill 889 imposed a one-year moratorium on the reappraisal that took effect January 1, 2026, and the county says it applies to Guilford.

The state Department of Revenue had ordered the reappraisal in April 2023, because most Guilford parcels were selling for more than their assessed value. County appraisers did the work in-house, and notices went out in February 2026. The county says the next reappraisal is set for 2032.

Owners who appealed the 2026 value did not lose the appeal. The county states that pending appeals are still processed and apply to the following year's bill. Commissioners adopted a rate of 78.95 cents per $100 of assessed value for fiscal year 2026-27, an increase of 5.9 cents. The rate rose in 2026 and the values rise in 2027, so the two changes reach your bill in separate years.

sections.h2: When are Guilford County property taxes due and when does interest start?
sections.html:
State law makes the bill payable September 1, and it stays at face value through January 5. From January 6 interest runs. Guilford's own FAQ puts the cutoff at January 5 and says bills usually arrive in the first two weeks of July.

The county rewards early payment. Its FAQ prints a 0.5% discount for paying by August 31, while the county's 2026 moratorium notice told residents that paying by Monday, August 31, 2026 still earned a 1% discount. Ask the Tax Department which percentage applies to the bill in your hand.

Once the delinquent date passes, interest is 2% for the first month and 0.75% for each month after. The county adds that enforcement starts right away. Its FAQ lists wage garnishment, bank levies, personal property seizure, attachment of state tax refunds and lottery winnings, and foreclosure. The Tax Department says it does not hold tax lien sales.

A mailed payment counts on the postmark date. If the postmark is missing or not from the Postal Service, the date the office receives it controls, and the taxpayer carries the burden of proving timely payment.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Guilford County property value?
sections.html:
File a written appeal with the Board of Equalization and Review, normally between January 1 and May 15 at 5 p.m. Online filing is allowed, and a paper form can be requested at 336-641-4814. A weekend or holiday deadline slides to the next business day.

Because of the moratorium, the county's board page says 2026 appeals could be filed through December 31, 2026, and 2027 appeals can be filed through May 17, 2027, with the online portal opening January 1, 2027. Email taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov if you want a form before then.

After you file, an appraiser reviews the parcel and sends a recommendation. Accept it and no hearing is needed. Reject it and you get a date to present evidence to the five-member board. The county's assessed value is presumed correct, so the burden sits with the owner. Guilford's board page describes what counts:

  • Sales of similar homes near the reappraisal date, an appraisal from the prior year, or a contractor estimate for a defect.
  • Square footage or property record card errors, and outside factors such as a flood zone.

The board does not accept the size of a tax increase or a taxpayer's inability to pay as a reason, and it does not treat foreclosure sales as comparables. Expect a written decision within roughly two weeks of the hearing. The next step is the state Property Tax Commission, and notice of that appeal is due within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

sections.h2: Which Guilford County tax relief programs can lower the bill before a sale?
sections.html:
Three programs exist, and an owner may receive only one. The county takes applications through June 1 each year, and later ones go to the Board of Equalization and Review if the packet arrives at least a week before the board's final December meeting.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of the home's value comes off the taxable amount. The owner must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled as of January 1. The county prints an income cap of $38,800, and owners apply once.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: bills are capped at 4% of income, or 5% when income runs above $38,800 up to $58,200. The owner must have lived in the home five years, and the application repeats every year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of value is excluded with no age or income test, for a veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability or an unmarried surviving spouse.

The circuit breaker matters most to sellers. The deferred amount is a lien, and a transfer of the property makes the last three years of deferred tax payable with interest, so expect that amount to come due on the transfer date. The exclusions do not have to be repaid. Applications go to PO Box 3138, Greensboro, NC 27402, or by hand to either tax office; call 336-641-3320 or 336-641-7911 with questions.

sections.h2: What should a Guilford County seller do about unpaid property tax?
sections.html:
Pay it off from the sale or before it. State law puts the tax lien on each parcel as of the January 1 listing date, with penalties and interest attached at the same moment, so a buyer's title search will find it.

If your lender escrows taxes, the Tax Department says the servicer asks the county for the bill and mails you a notice around mid to late July. The notice does not shift the legal duty to you, so check that the servicer paid the right amount. A home without escrow needs a direct payment before the interest date.

A tax foreclosure runs through the courts as an action like a mortgage foreclosure, with a public sale at the courthouse door and a 10-day window after the sale report for an increased bid. Selling before that point keeps the sale price in your hands. Check the Tax Department's parcel and bill search for the exact payoff, and ask the register of deeds how the deed will record. Our Guilford County register of deeds guide covers that step.

Three items worth checking before a Guilford house is listed:

  • A circuit breaker deferment that comes due on transfer.
  • A parcel record that does not match the house after an addition. The county accepts a Property Verification form online and says record cards update in about 48 hours.
  • Vehicle gap bills, which are billed separately from the real estate bill.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Guilford County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists 246,403 housing units as of July 1, 2025, and 219,718 households for 2020 to 2024. Owners occupy 59.9% of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $259,900.

Median monthly owner costs are $1,536 with a mortgage and $515 without one, and median gross rent is $1,163. The median household income is $68,642 in 2024 dollars. Builders pulled 2,876 permits in 2025, and 85.1% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which describes a county where most owners stay put. Persons 65 and older make up 18.0% of the population, the group the relief programs above are written for.

faqs.q: Did Guilford County use the 2026 reappraisal values on the 2026 tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 bill used 2025 assessed values because of the moratorium in Senate Bill 889, and the new values apply to the 2027 bill. The county says the next reappraisal is scheduled for 2032, and appeals filed against the 2026 values are still processed.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Guilford County property value?
faqs.a: May 15 at 5 p.m. in a normal year, and an appeal must be received or postmarked by then. Under the moratorium the county's board page says 2026 appeals ran through December 31, 2026 and 2027 appeals run through May 17, 2027.

faqs.q: Can a senior or veteran in Guilford County get a lower property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 or older or totally disabled with income under the cap can exclude the greater of $25,000 or half the home's value, and a veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability can exclude $45,000. Apply to the Tax Department by June 1.

faqs.q: What happens to taxes deferred under the circuit breaker if I sell?
faqs.a: They become due. A transfer of the home is a disqualifying event, and the last three years of deferred tax come due with interest on the transfer date. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff figure before closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Guilford County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay online or by phone through the Pay It portal, by mail to P.O. Box 70939 in Charlotte, or in person at the Greensboro or High Point tax office. Cards carry a processing fee, and the county does not accept gift cards.
